mainTopic: Disqualifications of the סוטה's scroll, unresolved questions about mixing and drinking the water, the wording of the two oaths, and the משנה on her double אָמֵן.
overview: This amud finishes a list of things that make the סוטה's scroll unfit: writing it on two separate pages, or writing and erasing it one letter at a time. Then רבא asks a chain of questions about two סוטות whose scrolls are erased into one cup, or erased separately and then mixed, or mixed and then split again. The last of these depends on ברירה, and the chain ends in תיקו. רבא and רב אשי ask more questions about how she drinks: through a fiber or tube, or when some of the water spilled. These also end in תיקו. Next, רב explains that the two oaths in the פסוקים come before and after the erasing. רבא rejects this and says one oath has a curse with it and one does not. רב, רבא and רב אשי then argue about the exact wording of an oath with a curse. Finally a new משנה begins, explaining everything her double אָמֵן covers.

steps.title: Writing the scroll on two pages makes it unfit
steps.stepSummary: If the סוטה's scroll is written on two separate pages, it is פסולה, because the תורה says 'ספר', meaning one scroll.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote it on two pages, it is unfit. The תורה said 'a scroll', meaning one scroll and not two or three scrolls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a list of things that make the סוטה's scroll unfit. Here it rules that the scroll must be on one piece, not on two pages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the singular word 'ספר' in the פסוק. One scroll means one connected writing surface. Two separate pages count as two scrolls, so the scroll is פסול.

phrases.english: If he wrote it on two pages, it is unfit.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the סוטה's scroll with the curses that later gets erased into the water.

phrases.english: The Merciful One said 'scroll', meaning one,
and not two or three scrolls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier list of disqualifications for the מגילת סוטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוטה scroll written on two separate pages is פסולה, based on the singular word 'ספר'.

steps.title: Writing and erasing letter by letter makes it unfit
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן writes one letter and erases it, then writes another and erases it, the scroll is פסולה. The whole פרשה must be written first and then erased.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he wrote one letter and erased it, then wrote another letter and erased it, it is unfit. The פסוק says, 'And the priest shall do to her all of this law.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way the scroll becomes unfit: writing and erasing one letter at a time instead of writing it all and then erasing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'כל התורה הזאת', all of this law. That teaches that the whole text must exist complete as one unit before it is erased. Erasing bit by bit means the full scroll never existed at one time.

keyTerms.meaning: 'All of this law', the whole procedure as one complete unit

steps.whatToRemember: The סוטה's scroll must be one scroll, fully written, and only then erased.

phrases.aramaic: כָּתַב אוֹת אַחַת וּמָחַק אוֹת אַחַת,
phrases.english: If he wrote one letter and erased one letter,

phrases.aramaic: וְכָתַב אוֹת אַחַת וּמָחַק אוֹת אַחַת
phrases.english: and wrote one letter and erased one letter
it is unfit, as it is written:
"And the priest shall do to her
all of this law."

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתַב אוֹת אַחַת וּמָחַק אוֹת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second disqualification to the same list, this one about the order of writing and erasing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Writing and erasing letter by letter makes the scroll פסולה; the whole text must be written before it is erased.

steps.title: Two scrolls for two women erased into one cup
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if two scrolls were written for two different סוטות but erased together into one cup, is it valid? It depends on whether only the writing must be לשמה or the erasing must be too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if he wrote two scrolls for two סוטות and erased them into one cup, what is the law? Do we only need the writing to be for her, which happened here? Or do we also need the erasing to be for her?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question about two women whose scrolls get erased into the same cup of water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each scroll was written for a specific woman, so the writing was לשמה. The open question is whether the erasing must also be done for one specific woman. If it must, erasing both scrolls together into one cup fails that requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a dilemma (a real open question)
For her sake, done for this specific woman
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to anything earlier. It is a real 'בעיא', an open question where רבא does not yet know the answer.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
If he wrote two scrolls for two sotah women,
and erased them into one cup, what is the law?
Do we require writing for her sake, and that is present here,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא בָּעֵינַן נָמֵי מְחִיקָה לִשְׁמָהּ?
phrases.english: or perhaps we also require erasing for her sake?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the list of disqualifications: the לשמה requirement when two women are involved.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the לשמה requirement apply only to writing the scroll, or also to erasing it?

steps.title: Erased in separate cups, then mixed together
steps.stepSummary: רבא's follow-up: even if erasing must be לשמה, what if each scroll was erased in its own cup and then the cups were mixed? Is separate erasing enough, or is it a problem that each woman drinks water that is not only hers?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say we also need erasing for her sake: if he erased them in two cups and then mixed them, what is the law? Do we need the erasing to be for her, which happened here? Or perhaps this one is not drinking her own water, and that one is not drinking her own water?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא builds a second question on top of the first. He assumes erasing must be לשמה and asks about a case where the erasing was done properly but the waters were mixed afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both the writing and the erasing were done separately for each woman. The new issue is the drinking: after mixing, each woman drinks water that also contains the other woman's scroll. The question is whether that makes the water unfit. Neither question gets an answer: the whole chain ends in תיקו in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say, assuming one side of the first question to ask a further one

steps.whyThisMatters: These questions show how far the לשמה idea reaches in the סוטה procedure: writing, erasing, and possibly even drinking water that belongs only to her.

phrases.english: And if you will say
we also require erasing for her sake,

phrases.aramaic: מְחָקָן בִּשְׁתֵּי כוֹסוֹת וְחָזַר וְעֵירְבָן, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: if he erased them in two cups and then mixed them, what is the law?
Do we require erasing for her sake, and that is present here,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא הָא לָאו דִּידַהּ קָא שָׁתְיָא
phrases.english: or perhaps this one is not drinking her own,
phrases.notes: 'Her own' means water that has only her scroll in it.

phrases.english: and that one is not drinking her own?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר בָּעֵינַן נָמֵי מְחִיקָה לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the stricter side of step 3, that erasing must be לשמה, and asks a further question about mixing after a proper erasing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If the erasing was לשמה but the waters were then mixed, is the water still valid, or must each woman drink only water from her own scroll?

steps.title: Mixed water that was split back into two cups
steps.stepSummary: רבא's third question: if the two mixed cups were divided again, can we say each woman got her own water (ברירה)? Unresolved: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the mixed water is a problem because this woman isn't drinking only her own water and that woman isn't drinking only her own water, what if the כהן divided it again into two cups? Is there ברירה or not? It stays unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds one more level to his question about two סוטות whose water got mixed. Now the mixed water is split back into two cups, and he asks if that fixes the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose mixing is a problem because each woman drinks someone else's water too. If the water is split again, we could say through ברירה that it is now clear each cup held that woman's own water. Or we could say there is no ברירה, so the water stays mixed and the problem remains. The question is never answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Looking back and saying that what happened later shows what was true from the start (here, which water belonged to which woman)
He went back and divided them again

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'no'. It means the גמרא found no answer, so the question stays open.

phrases.english: And if you say
this one is not drinking only her own water
and that one is not drinking only her own water,
if he went back and divided them, what is the law?
phrases.notes: This is the water that was mixed together in the last step, now poured back into two cups.

phrases.english: Is there ברירה, or is there no ברירה?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר הָא לָאו דִּידַהּ קָא שָׁתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third level to רבא's chain: if mixing is a problem, does splitting the water again fix it?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether splitting mixed water back into two cups counts, through ברירה, as each woman drinking her own water

steps.title: Drinking through a palm fiber or a tube
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether the סוטה's drinking counts if she drinks through a palm fiber or a tube. Unresolved: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if he made her drink through a palm fiber, what is the law? Through a tube, what is the law? Is that a normal way of drinking, or not? It stays unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a new question about the way the סוטה drinks the water. Does it count if she drinks it through a fiber or a tube instead of from the cup?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the כהן makes her drink. If drinking through a fiber or tube is a normal way to drink, it counts. If it is not normal, the drinking might not count. The גמרא leaves this unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question (raised a dilemma)

phrases.english: Rava asked:
If he made her drink through a palm fiber, what is the law?
Through a tube, what is the law?
Is this a normal way of drinking,
or is this not a normal way of drinking?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from mixed cups to a new topic: the way she drinks.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether drinking through a fiber or tube counts as normal drinking for the סוטה

steps.title: When some of the water spilled
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks what the law is if some of the water spilled and only some was left. Unresolved: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: if some of the water spilled and some was left, what is the law? It stays unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks one more question about the drinking. If part of the water spilled, can she drink what is left?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether she must drink all the water that the scroll was erased into, or whether drinking part of it is enough. Since spilled water can't be drunk, the answer decides if the leftover water still works. This also ends in תיקו.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
If some of the water spilled and some of it was left, what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי: נִשְׁפְּכוּ מֵהֶן וְנִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ מֵהֶן, מַהוּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another unresolved question about the act of drinking, this time about how much water she drinks.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether drinking only the remaining part of the water is enough
steps.whatToRemember: Steps 5 to 7 are three open questions, all ending in תיקו: water split again after mixing (ברירה), drinking through a fiber or tube, and water that partly spilled.

steps.title: Why the סוטה has two oaths
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא in the name of רב: the תורה mentions two oaths for the סוטה, one before the scroll is erased and one after.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב: why are two oaths stated about the סוטה? One is before the scroll is erased, and one is after it is erased.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רב explains why the תורה mentions the oath for the סוטה twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוטה section in the תורה says twice that the כהן makes her swear. רב says this is not extra: each one is a separate oath at a different time. One comes before the מגילה is erased into the water and one after.

keyTerms.meaning: The scroll with the סוטה section written on it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is רב's reading only. In the very next step רבא rejects it, because the פסוקים place both oaths before the erasing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav said:
The two oaths that are stated about the sota.
Why are there two?
One is before the scroll is erased,
and one is after it is erased.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב: שְׁתֵּי שְׁבוּעוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בַּסּוֹטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the unresolved drinking questions and begins a new statement about the oaths.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוטה swears twice: once before the scroll is erased and once after.

steps.title: רבא: both oaths come before the erasing
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the view from the previous step that one oath is said after the מגילה is erased.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objects: Both oaths are written before the scroll is erased!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the previous statement, which said that one oath comes before the erasing and one comes after. He points out that the תורה writes both oaths before it mentions the erasing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step needed a reason why the תורה mentions two oaths, and it answered with timing: one before the erasing, one after. רבא says the order of the פסוקים does not allow this, because both oaths appear before the erasing. So the reason for two oaths must be something other than timing.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it; attacks the previous statement
Was erased (the scroll with the curses)

phrases.english: Rava objects to it:
Both of them are written before the scroll was erased!
phrases.notes: Look at במדבר 5:19–23. Both oaths come in the פסוקים first, and only afterward does it say to erase the scroll.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's statement in the name of רב that one oath is said after the erasing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the second oath is said after the מגילה is erased.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The order of the פסוקים places both oaths before the erasing, so the timing explanation does not fit the text.

steps.title: רבא's new explanation: one oath with a curse, one without
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the two oaths differ in content: one has an אלה attached and one does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: One is an oath that has a curse with it, and one is an oath that has no curse with it.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the timing explanation, רבא offers his own reason for the two oaths. The difference is what is in each oath, not when it is said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both oaths come before she drinks. One is a plain שבועה, and the other is a שבועה joined to an אלה (curse). This sets up the next question: what exactly does an oath with a curse sound like?
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the two oaths differ in content (with a curse or without one), not in timing.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
One is an oath that has a curse with it,
and one is an oath that has no curse with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that רבא just rejected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה's two oaths are one oath with a curse and one oath without a curse.

steps.title: What does an oath with a curse sound like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact wording of the oath that comes with a curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the circumstances of an oath that has a curse with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how an oath with a curse is actually worded. This sets up the three answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's idea depends on knowing what makes an oath count as having a curse with it. The rest of the passage is a series of attempts to get this wording right.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances
of an oath that has a curse with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of רבא's explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact wording the כהן uses for an oath that comes with a curse.

steps.title: רב's wording: oath, then a separate curse
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם in the name of רב gives the wording: I make you swear you were not defiled, for if you were, the curses will come upon you.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said in the name of רב: The כהן says, 'I make you swear that you were not defiled, for if you were defiled, they will come upon you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first version of the wording. The כהן makes her swear she is innocent, and then adds that the curses will come if she is guilty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the oath is about her innocence, and the curse is given as the reason ('for if...'). The two parts sit next to each other, which is exactly what רבא will criticize next.

keyTerms.meaning: They will come upon you (the curses)

phrases.english: Rav Amram said that Rav said:
'I make you swear that you were not defiled,'
'for if you were defiled, they will come upon you.'
phrases.notes: The word 'they' means the curses of the סוטה, which the text does not spell out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how the oath with a curse is worded.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The oath is that she was not defiled, followed by 'for if you were defiled, the curses will come upon you.'

steps.title: רבא: the curse and the oath are separate
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that in רב's wording the curse and the oath are two separate statements.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The curse stands by itself, and the oath stands by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא says רב's wording does not really make one oath with a curse inside it. It is an oath, and then a curse said next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For it to be an oath 'with' a curse, the curse has to be part of what she swears to. In רב's version the oath covers only 'I was not defiled', and the curse is just added on as a reason.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The curse stands by itself
and the oath stands by itself!

steps.kashyaTarget: רב's wording of the oath with a curse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The curse is not part of the oath. The two are separate statements, so this is not truly an oath with a curse.

steps.title: רבא's wording: swear that the curses will come
steps.stepSummary: רבא puts the curse inside the oath: I make you swear that if you were defiled, the curses will come upon you.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The כהן says, 'I make you swear that if you were defiled, they will come upon you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא fixes the wording so that the oath itself is about the curse. She swears to accept the curse if she is guilty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the words 'I make you swear' lead straight into the curse, so the oath and the curse are one statement. But the line 'that you were not defiled' has dropped out, which sets up רב אשי's objection.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
'I make you swear'
'that if you were defiled, they will come upon you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new wording that answers רבא's own objection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An oath followed by a separate curse counts as an oath with a curse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The curse must be the content of the oath itself.

steps.title: רב אשי: now there is a curse but no oath
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects that רבא's wording has a curse but no real oath about her innocence.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: There is a curse, but there is no oath!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי says רבא's version went too far. It has the curse but no longer has her swearing that she was not defiled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath needs something she swears to, here her innocence. רבא's wording only says the curses will come if she was defiled, so the actual oath is missing.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
There is a curse, but there is no oath!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אָלָה אִיכָּא שְׁבוּעָה לֵיכָּא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's wording of the oath with a curse.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leaving out 'that you were not defiled' removes the oath about her innocence.

steps.title: רב אשי's wording: oath and curse joined together
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי combines both parts: I make you swear that you were not defiled, and that if you were, the curses will come upon you.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: The כהן says, 'I make you swear that you were not defiled, and that if you were defiled, they will come upon you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the final wording. The oath covers both her innocence and the curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using 'and if' instead of 'for if' makes the curse a second part of the same oath, not a separate reason. This keeps the oath of innocence that רבא dropped and the joined curse that רב lacked.

keyTerms.meaning: And if (joining the curse into the same oath)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three versions of the wording. רב: oath plus a separate curse. רבא: swear to the curse only. רב אשי: swear to innocence and to the curse together, in one oath.
steps.confusionAlert: רב's and רב אשי's wordings look almost the same. The only difference is 'שֶׁאִם' (for if), which gives a separate reason, versus 'וְאִם' (and if), which adds the curse into the oath.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
'I make you swear that you were not defiled,'
'and that if you were defiled, they will come upon you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's own objection with a combined wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the formula so it includes both parts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Swearing only to the curse is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oath must include both her innocence and the curse, joined together as one oath.

steps.title: What the double אָמֵן covers
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that the סוטה's double אָמֵן takes in several things: the curse and the oath, this man and any other man, and her time as a ארוסה and as a נשואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: What is she agreeing to when she says 'אָמֵן, אָמֵן'? אָמֵן to the curse, and אָמֵן to the oath. אָמֵן about this man, and אָמֵן about any other man. אָמֵן that I did not stray while I was betrothed or while I was married.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It asks why the פסוק has the סוטה say 'אָמֵן' twice, and begins listing everything her אָמֵן includes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled word tells us her answer covers more than one thing. The first pair matches what we just learned: the כהן's words contain both an אָלָה (curse) and a שבועה (oath), and she accepts both. The משנה then widens her אָמֵן to include other men, not only the man she was warned about, and both stages of marriage, ארוסה and נשואה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So be it.' Saying it means accepting the oath and curse as if she said them herself
Curse. The punishment she accepts if she is guilty
Oath. Her statement that she is innocent
I strayed. Taken from the פסוק's wording 'כי שטית' (if you have strayed)
A woman who is betrothed but has not yet married and moved in
A woman who is fully married

steps.whatToRemember: Her double אָמֵן is not a repeat. Each אָמֵן adds coverage: the curse and the oath, this man and other men, and her time as a ארוסה and as a נשואה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אָמֵן מֵאִישׁ זֶה / אָמֵן מֵאִישׁ אַחֵר' does not mean two different men spoke to her. It means her oath covers being with the man she was warned about AND being with any other man.
steps.whyThisMatters: The first pair, curse and oath, shows that the כהן's words contain both an אָלָה and a שבועה, the same two elements the earlier steps were discussing.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
On what does she say
'Amen, amen'?
Amen on the curse,
amen on the oath.
Amen regarding this man,
phrases.notes: The man her husband warned her about.

phrases.english: amen regarding another man.
Amen that I did not stray
as a betrothed woman or as a married woman

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. Its first pair (curse and oath) matches the distinction between an oath and a curse discussed in steps 10–16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The double אָמֵן of the סוטה covers the curse and the oath, the warned-about man and any other man, and straying as a ארוסה or as a נשואה.
